throughline: The Mandukya Upanishad maps the syllable Om to waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, pointing to a silent fourth state of pure awareness.
title: The Four Quarters of Om
description: This script explores the Mandukya Upanishad's teaching that the syllable Om corresponds to the three states of consciousness. It explains how A, U, and M represent waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, while the silence after the sound points to the fourth quarter, Turiya, as described in the text.
assumptions: The interpretation relies on the Mandukya Upanishad and its traditional commentaries.
The visual representation of Om is symbolic, not a literal acoustic diagram.
The fourth state is presented as a philosophical concept, not a scientific claim.

scenes.title: Hook
cues: Have you ever wondered why the Om symbol is considered sacred?
scenes.visualIntent: The Devanagari glyph for Om appears clearly in the center, static and distinct against a dark background.

scenes.title: Mystery
cues: How can one simple syllable map the entire range of your daily human experience?
The Mandukya Upanishad suggests it contains the key to understanding your own consciousness.
scenes.visualIntent: Subtle, slow ripples emanate from the center of the Om glyph, suggesting an inner expansion rather than physical sound waves.

scenes.title: Explanation
cues: The text links the first sound, A, to your waking state, where you perceive the world.
The middle sound, U, corresponds to the dream state, where your mind turns inward.
The final sound, M, represents deep sleep, a state of rest without distinct objects.
These three sounds together describe the common experiences of every human being.
Meditating on this sequence helps the seeker recognize the Self across all states.
scenes.visualIntent: The letters A, U, and M appear sequentially next to the Om glyph, each with a small label: Waking, Dream, Deep Sleep.

scenes.title: Payoff
cues: But the teaching points beyond these three to a fourth, silent quarter called Turiya.
This is not deep sleep, but the awareness that remains when all sounds and states dissolve.
The silence after Om is the symbol for this underlying, non-dual reality.
scenes.visualIntent: The A, U, and M labels fade away, leaving only the Om glyph, which then settles into a still, soundless visual state.

scenes.title: Ending
cues: When the sound fades, what are you still aware of?
scenes.visualIntent: The Om glyph remains centered, with a gentle, contemplative focus, inviting the viewer to reflect on their own awareness.
